scene.note: server.js now looks at what each request asks for and answers each address in its own way, or says plainly what was wrong.

steps.note: A request arrives, and the server looks at its path.
The noticeboard team asks for the whole list, and gets every plot with its holder.
A phone at the gate asks for the free plots, as before.
The bare address gets a welcome that names the other two.
Someone types an address the server does not have.
The server says the page is not there, with a status every program understands.
Another program tries to change the plot list, which can only be read.
The server says that method is not allowed there, and which one is.
Someone by the tap asks for the free plots, with their row in the query.
The server takes the path alone to choose the route, and reads the row with the URL tools.
Only the free plots of that row are answered, or a line saying the row has none.
